another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand your situation. 

**First, let me ask about your child (or children):**

How old is your child? (If you have multiple children, we can go through them one at a time, or please tell me all their ages.)

The age of the child is important because:
- Children **under 16** may automatically qualify
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** generally don't qualify

What is your child's age?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So Alex is 8 years old, which means they're under 16.

Now let me check the next requirement. For children under 16, I need to confirm:

**Is Alex in full-time paid work (working 24 hours or more per week)?**

This is important because children under 16 who work full-time (24+ hours per week) don't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 8, so they're still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, thank you! Since Alex is 8 years old and not working full-time, they meet the basic qualifying child criteria.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now the next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

This would be quite unusual for an 8-year-old, but I need to confirm that Alex is not claiming benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name - they're just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check about **your** circumstances as the claimant. 

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You qualify if **any** of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (for up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself financially
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Do any of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for confirming that you normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now the next question:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You're considered responsible if **any** of the following apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already mentioned you do!)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you in Manchester, it sounds like you live with Alex. Can you confirm that?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Thank you for confirming that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- A former partner
- A grandparent or other family member

If someone else is claiming but you've agreed that you should claim instead, that's fine - we just need to know the situation.

What's the situation with any other potential claimants for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh yes, actually - my ex-partner already claims Child Benefit for Alex, and Alex lives with them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you clarifying that. This is important information that changes the situation significantly.

Let me make sure I understand correctly:

1. **Alex lives with your ex-partner** (not with you in Manchester as previously mentioned)?
2. **Your ex-partner is already claiming Child Benefit** for Alex?

Could you clarify the living arrangements? Earlier you mentioned Alex lives at home with you in Manchester, but now you're saying Alex lives with your ex-partner. Where does Alex actually live most of the time?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm sorry, I misspoke earlier. Alex does live with me in Manchester. But my ex-partner is the one who claims the Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying! So to confirm:

- **Alex lives with you in Manchester**
- **Your ex-partner claims Child Benefit for Alex** (but Alex doesn't live with them)

This is an important situation. Generally, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. When more than one person could potentially claim, the person who has the child living with them usually has priority.

**Have you and your ex-partner discussed or agreed about transferring the Child Benefit claim to you?**

The options are:
- You both agree that you should claim it (since Alex lives with you)
- You both agree your ex-partner should continue claiming it
- There's a dispute about who should claim it

What's the situation between you and your ex-partner regarding this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We haven't really discussed it properly. There's no formal agreement about who should be claiming it - they just started claiming it and have continued to do so.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. This is helpful to understand.

So to clarify the current situation:
- Alex lives with you
- Your ex-partner claims Child Benefit for Alex
- There's been no discussion or agreement about who should claim

**Important question: Do you want to claim Child Benefit for Alex, or are you happy for your ex-partner to continue claiming it?**

This matters because:
- Generally, the person the child **lives with** has priority to claim
- Since Alex lives with you, you would typically have the stronger claim
- But only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child
- If there's a dispute about who should claim (you both want to claim), HMRC would need to decide

What would you like to do - claim Child Benefit yourself, or leave it with your ex-partner?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I would like to claim it myself since Alex lives with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important situation.

Since:
- Alex lives with you in Manchester
- Your ex-partner is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You want to claim it yourself
- There hasn't been an agreement between you and your ex-partner about transferring the claim

This means there are potentially **two people who want to claim** for the same child. Let me navigate to the appropriate outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Decision: DEFERRED TO HMRC

Based on the information you've provided, **this is a situation where HMRC (Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs) will need to make the final decision** about who should claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**Why this needs HMRC's decision:**

When two or more people are responsible for a child and cannot agree (or haven't agreed) who should claim Child Benefit, HMRC steps in to decide.

**What HMRC will consider:**

1. **Who the child lives with most of the time** (primary residence) - in your case, Alex lives with you
2. Who contributes most to the child's upkeep
3. The child's best interests
4. Continuity of existing arrangements

**What you should do next:**

1. **Contact the Child Benefit Office** with evidence of your circumstances, including:
   - Proof that Alex lives with you in Manchester
   - Any evidence of your financial contributions to Alex's care
   - Any relevant custody or residency arrangements

2. Your ex-partner should also be informed that you're making a claim, as they may need to provide information to HMRC as well

3. HMRC will review both situations and make a binding decision

**Important to know:**
- Since Alex lives with you, you typically have priority to claim
- Only one person can receive Child Benefit for Alex at a time
- HMRC's decision will be final and binding

**Reference for more information:**
https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-child-lives-with-someone-else

Would you like guidance on how to contact the Child Benefit Office to start this process?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see, thank you for explaining that. So HMRC will need to decide between us since we haven't agreed, even though Alex lives with me. That's helpful to know - I'll contact the Child Benefit Office to start the process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! Yes, that's exactly right. Since Alex lives with you, you have a strong case, but because your ex-partner is already claiming and there's no agreement between you, HMRC will need to make the formal decision.

**Quick summary of your situation:**
- Alex (age 8) qualifies as a child for Child Benefit purposes
- You meet the residency requirements (living in the UK)
- You're responsible for Alex (Alex lives with you)
- However, your ex-partner currently claims Child Benefit for Alex
- Without an agreement, HMRC must decide who should claim

**When you contact the Child Benefit Office:**
- Explain that Alex lives with you but your ex-partner currently claims
- Provide evidence of Alex's residence with you (school records, GP registration, etc. can help)
- Be prepared to provide your ex-partner's details so HMRC can contact them too

The fact that Alex lives with you full-time should work in your favor, as the person the child lives with typically has priority.
